newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX index ends bourse stable, higher.
newsitem.headline: German DAX index ends bourse stable, higher.

text.p: German shares defied forecasts of a lower start to the week to end bourse on Monday stable at higher levels, as traders incorporated the possible effect of a rise in U.S. interest rates into their trading strategies.
The DAX index of 30 blue-chip shares ended at 3,321.84 points, up 23.60 points or 0.72 percent, while the June DAX future was up 3,334 points, up 29 points.
"The market is suprisingly strong this morning. The main factor is that the market has factored in a 25-basis point hike in U.S. interest rates," said a Frankfurt trader.

Speculation of a possible interest rate hike intensified last week after comments by the chairman of the U.S. Federal Reserve, Alan Greenspan, which were interpreted by market players as pointing towards a rise in key rates.

At the end of bourse trade in Frankfurt, engineer Thyssen AG, was up 26.50 marks, or 8.08 pct at 417.50 marks, rising on reports it was planning to tell shareholders its shares have the potential to reach a price of around 550 marks.
Last week Krupp-Hoesch announced a takeover bid. Since then Thyssen agreed to discuss a joint steel company. If the talks fail, Krupp said it planned to reinstate the offer.
Krupp also benefited from the reports, and rose to end bourse up 21.50 marks, or 6.78 percent, at 338.50 marks.
Other corporate news in early trade included Deutsche Bank AG denying it had an agreement to "pool" its 25.8 percent in builder Philipp Holzmann AG with a stake held by Hochtief AG.
The bank did say it was in discussion with Hochtief on pooling their stakes.
Holzmann shares ended up 29 marks, over 5.5 percent, at 549 marks, while Hochtief shares ended up 1.20 marks, 1.70 percent, at 71.40 marks.
